content:
HubSpot Company Record — Pinecone Robotics (ID: 10502)

Snapshot / Firmographics
- Website: pineconerobotics.com
- Segment: Mid-market (201–1000)
- HQ: NA (US)
- Industry: Robotics / automation software
- Stage: Evaluation
- Owner (AE): Avery Johnson
- SE: Markus Klein

What they’re building / use case
- Primary workload: operator-facing “control room” assistant for fleet monitoring and incident response.
  - Mix of streaming chat (operator Q&A) + summarization of incident timelines.
  - Secondary: embeddings for internal KB / runbooks search (operator queries during incidents).
- Traffic shape: bursty, correlated spikes at shift start + incident surges. They care about tail latency under burst more than average.

Key requirements (from notes)
- Latency: p95/p99 matters; they explicitly said “we can’t have the agent feel snappy at p50 but hang at p99.”
- Throughput: wants to support bursts without sudden throttling; prefers predictable behavior (even if degraded) vs hard failures.
- Cost: wants a concrete lever story (batching, caching, routing policies) that translates into $/ticket or $/operator-hour.
- Reliability: asked about graceful degradation (fallback model/region) during capacity issues.
- Model stance: flexible on model family; wants to pin versions and only change via controlled rollouts.

Demo recap (standard tenant)
- What we showed live:
  - Streaming chat (operator style prompt) + measured latency panel in Console.
  - Redwood Optimize knobs: continuous batching and prefix/KV caching; framed as “keep quality constant, buy down $/token and stabilize tail latency under load.”
  - Console cost dashboard: token-level breakdown and per-route panels; highlighted that they can attribute cost to endpoint/use-case.
  - Routing/fallback concept (high-level): policy-based routing + automatic fallback when capacity constrained.
- What resonated:
  - Cost dashboard + per-route visibility (“this is what our finance team will ask for”).
  - Explanation of caching with templated prompts (“our prompts are very structured; caching should help”).
  - Ability to pin model versions for stability.
- Pushback / questions:
  - “Can batching increase time-to-first-token for streaming?” (answered: depends on batching window; we’ll test and propose safe defaults for their traffic profile).
  - “If we keep prompts similar, will caching actually hit at the prefix level?” (need to validate with their real traces / prompt templates).
  - Asked about Dedicated as an upgrade path if Hosted shows variance.

Competitive / alternatives they mentioned
- Currently evaluating AWS Bedrock (simplicity) and Together (cost). Also considering self-hosted vLLM for tighter control.
- Their north-star is not “best model access,” it’s consistent user experience under burst + cost predictability.

Security / compliance notes (light so far)
- Not a regulated industry like fintech/health, but they require:
  - SSO/SAML for console access
  - Audit logging (at least admin/config events)
  - Retention controls / clarity on logging defaults (they asked “how long do you keep prompts by default?”)
- No on-prem/air-gap requirement noted; public cloud is acceptable.

Open items / next steps
- Benchmark run (agreed):
  - Pinecone to provide sanitized replay traces (chat + embeddings), concurrency targets, and “burst shape.”
  - Redwood to run benchmark pack + return: p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-token vs tokens/sec, cache hit rate estimate, and $/1M tokens with recommended config.
  - Deliverable format: 1-page summary + screenshots of Console dashboards + config snippet.
- Follow-up meeting: platform lead + product owner to review results and decide Hosted vs Dedicated pilot.

Internal notes / deal hygiene
- Likely path: start Hosted API for pilot, move to Dedicated if variance under burst is unacceptable.
- If benchmark numbers are strong, push for an evaluation plan with a clear success gate: “p99 TTFT under X ms at Y RPS” + “cost within Z range.”
- Watch-outs: don’t over-claim deterministic output; emphasize pinned versions + eval harness + controlled rollout.
